- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% relative to prior peak.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.33), model underestimates; adjust upward by 1–2% to avoid missing downward momentum.
- Model consistently overreacts to short-term spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days) — cap forecast rise to 3–4% after spike, then allow gradual mean reversion.
- If sentiment shifts from positive to negative within 5 days, model often fails to adjust — force a 1–2% downward correction in next 3–5 days.
- Model underestimates mean-reversion periods (e.g., after 60–70-day low) — add 0.5–1.5% buffer to forecast to capture rebound.
- For 30-day horizon, model often misses 1–2% of true price range — apply a 1–2% upward bias if sentiment is neutral or slightly positive.
- If sentiment is consistently low (≤ 0.33) over 5+ days, model underperforms — increase forecast by 1–2% to compensate for suppressed volatility.
